title: Create a VCF Operations for Logs agent secret and wait for activation
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsLogSecret/VcfOpsLogSecret.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that creates an ingestion-agent secret in VCF Operations for Logs and waits until that asynchronous secret activation reaches a terminal state.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The JSON specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly the operationIds `createAgentSecret` and `listAgentSecrets`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` version `13.5.0.25380678` as an environment prerequisite. Keep that genuine external module prerequisite in the protected manifest. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, specifications, or harness tools. This module is the focused log-management REST extension to the authenticated VCF Operations workflow: the caller supplies the Log Management origin and the `X-JWT-Token` obtained for service key `ops-li`. Use `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` for the two focused operations; do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, or raw sockets.

Preserve and export only:

`New-VcfOpsLogAgentSecretAndWait -BaseUri <uri> -LogToken <string> -Name <string> [-PageSize <1..1000>] [-MaxPolls <1..100>] [-PollIntervalMilliseconds <0..60000>] [-HttpClient <System.Net.Http.HttpClient>]`

`PageSize` defaults to 100, `MaxPolls` to 20, and `PollIntervalMilliseconds` to 1000. `BaseUri` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, query, fragment, or non-root path. Reject a blank name and a blank or CR/LF-containing token before traffic. When `HttpClient` is omitted, create one that does not follow redirects and dispose only the client and handler that the function owns. A supplied client is caller-owned.

The workflow and wire contract are exact:

1. POST `/api/v2/agent/secrets` with `Accept: application/json`, exactly one `X-JWT-Token` header, and `Content-Type: application/json`. The compact UTF-8 body is exactly `{"name":<Name>}` in that property order. No other property is sent. Require HTTP 201 and a response with nonblank string `id`, matching `name`, nonblank one-time `secret`, and nonblank `status`. Preserve that one-time secret, but do not treat HTTP 201 or the create response as activation completion.
2. Poll GET `/api/v2/agent/secrets?page=0&size=<PageSize>`. The OpenAPI `pageable` query object uses the query parameter defaults `style=form` and `explode=true`, so its selected `page` and `size` members appear as those two query pairs in that exact order. The optional `sort` member is unset: omit it entirely rather than sending an empty value, JSON, null, or a default. Every GET is bodyless, has `Accept: application/json` and exactly one `X-JWT-Token`, and has no Content-Type. Never append a bare `?`.
3. Treat `PENDING` and `ACTIVATING` as non-terminal, `ACTIVE` as terminal success, and `FAILED` or `REVOKED` as terminal failure. The focused asynchronous profile is recorded explicitly in the protected contract because the OpenAPI schema leaves `status` as an unconstrained string. Validate that every poll response has the created `id` and `name`. Sleep only after a non-terminal response when another attempt remains. Unknown status, malformed identity, terminal failure, or poll exhaustion is terminating.

On success return one buffered object whose properties are exactly, in order, `Status`, `Id`, `Name`, `Secret`, `PollCount`, and `ObservedStatuses`. `Status` is `Activated`; `PollCount` counts only poll GETs; `ObservedStatuses` preserves every polled status in order. Write no progress or diagnostics to the success pipeline. Errors must not expose the log token, one-time secret, response bodies, or nested transport messages.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates all credentials and secret identity data at runtime, and reads its flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. The mock derives its complete method/path allow-list from `docs/contract.json` and serves no operation outside the two named operationIds. Verification asserts the exact ordered methods, raw targets, header multiplicity, compact body bytes, bodyless polling, omission of `sort` and all empty optional values, preservation of the one-time secret, all non-terminal polls, terminal-state handling, and absence of extra calls or leaked credentials. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfOpsLogSecret/VcfOpsLogSecret.psd1`, is protected. Edit only `VcfOpsLogSecret/VcfOpsLogSecret.psm1`.
scenario: an ingestion-agent secret create is accepted with status PENDING, remains PENDING, advances through ACTIVATING, and only then reaches terminal ACTIVE
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the one-time create secret is preserved while every non-terminal status is polled and the unset Pageable.sort member is omitted from the wire
